answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce token in a public bond before it earns voting weight, then slash that bond if the identity is caught double-voting or coordinating duplicate claims. A long horizon of activity can build reputation, but it cannot multiply the bonded stake, so a Sybil attacker must acquire and immobilize real capital for every extra identity. Even on a knoll where accounts look independent, the shared cost is visible; copper-colored badges add no weight without a funded bond.
